planet.name: Mercury
planet.p: Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system and the closest to the Sun. It has no atmosphere to retain heat, causing extreme temperature swings between day and night.

planet.name: Venus
planet.p: Venus is the second planet from the Sun and the hottest in our solar system due to a thick, toxic atmosphere that traps heat. It rotates in the opposite direction to most planets.

planet.name: Mars
planet.p: Mars, known as the Red Planet, has a thin atmosphere and the largest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons. Evidence suggests it once had liquid water on its surface.

planet.name: Jupiter
planet.p: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system, a gas giant known for its Great Red Spot, a giant storm larger than Earth that has raged for centuries.

planet.name: Saturn
planet.p: Saturn is famous for its stunning ring system made of ice and rock particles. It is the least dense planet in our solar system and could theoretically float in water.

planet.name: Uranus
planet.p: Uranus is an ice giant that rotates on its side, likely due to a massive collision long ago. It has a faint ring system and appears pale blue due to methane in its atmosphere.

planet.name: Neptune
planet.p: Neptune is the farthest known planet from the Sun, a windy ice giant with the strongest winds in the solar system, reaching speeds of over 2,000 km/h.
